proof_steps: Assume SAT has circuits of size n^c in the stated model.
Apply the transfer theorem to obtain H_N circuits of size N^{q+beta c+o(1)}.
Compare this upper bound with the source lower bound N^a.
A contradiction is obtained exactly when q+beta c<a after absorbing o(1).
If beta>0 and a,q are fixed, sufficiently large c violates the inequality, so the route cannot establish all-exponent P/poly exclusion.
proof_packet.theorem_statement: Assume a route-specific transfer theorem: SAT in SIZE(n^c) implies SIZE(H_N)<=N^{q+beta c+o(1)} in the same model and without uncounted advice. If also SIZE(H_N)>N^a infinitely often or eventually on the same valid lengths, then the route contradicts SAT in SIZE(n^c) only when a>q+beta c.

theorem_scope.smallest_honest_claim: For a named P vs NP bridge route whose source carrier H_N is upper-bounded from SAT circuits by SIZE(H_N) <= N^{q+beta c+o(1)}, a barely-superlinear lower bound SIZE(H_N)>N^a rules out only target exponents c satisfying a>q+beta c. definition_fields.influence_closure: every row whose SAT value can change a FormulaEval line is included in the charged support
definition_fields.no_hidden_advice: row support cannot be supplied by nonuniform tables, semantic oracles, or private enable bits unless charged
definition_fields.row_enumeration_or_scan_charge: either RowSetEnumerator_N outputs selected rows with certified cost U_N or the parser pays the full scan charge F_FE N^{1+q+o(1)}
definition_fields.row_expansion_charge: each distinct selected row contributes the complete occurrence/SAT expansion term, typically N times the row count or T_N M_N in projected formulations
definition_fields.same_theory_parser: all support, selector, extension, and SAT occurrence conventions are read by the same proof verifier and circuit model
definition_fields.visible_selector_code: the proof displays the row predicate, extension rule, or enumerator certificate used to select rows

generic_countermodel_theorem.blocked_escape: RealSATInfluenceRealizer_N remains the only possible escape: it must force every semantically influential row into visible, charged support.
countermodel_spine: Choose a row r* not present in the parsed support Q_pi.
Let a hidden enable bit or semantic selector decide whether r* participates in FormulaEval.
Keep all displayed proof bits and charged occurrence neighborhoods fixed.
Flip the uncharged SAT/FormulaEval value at r*.
The parser outputs the same transcript while the selected support or H_N^SAT parity changes.
generic_countermodel_theorem.statement: If a FormulaEval mechanism lacks visible row support, selector extensionality, influence closure, or a charged semantic-realizer, then a private-row or unread-enable-bit construction gives two proof surfaces with the same parsed transcript but different FormulaEval dependence or carrier parity. Occurrence completion is therefore invalid.

examples_subsumed: projected guarded-dDNNF with witness or projected-enumerator charge
proof_spine: Parse all bEF, SATeq, bounded-SR_h, and extension dependencies into Gamma_bEF.
Use visible selector or enumerator fields to compute the complete FormulaEval row support or pay full scan.
Apply influence closure so every SAT row that can alter a FormulaEval line enters the charged support.
Expand each charged row into the same occurrence/SAT representation used by the carrier H_N^SAT.
Compose the public generator, parsed transcript, and residual patches into a nonuniform circuit for H_N^SAT.
Contradict LB_N(1+epsilon) exactly when the total size is subthreshold.
generic_positive_theorem.statement: If a Psys_sym FormulaEval mechanism satisfies TransparentRowSupport_N with discovery charge U_N, row-support size T_N, and FormulaEval expansion charge X_N, then the existing bEF parser extends to Gamma_trans(pi)=Gamma_bEF(pi)+U_N+X_N. If N^{rho+o(1)}+Gamma_trans(pi)<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}, the alleged LB_N(1+epsilon) certificate is falsified in the same nonuniform SIZE model.
